title: Preparation and Characterization of Paper Mill Sludge-based Co/Fe Composite Catalyst and the Influence of Various Inorganic Anions During the Fenton-like oxidation Process
content: Sewage sludge, particularly paper mill sludge, is carbonaceous by nature. It can be employed as a heterogeneous catalyst for Fenton-like reactions to attain high catalytic activity and long-term stability. In this paper, the Co/Fe bimetallic composite catalyst was prepared by taking paper mill sludge as the carrier via impregnation and calcination. This catalyst was employed to catalyze peroxymonosulfate (PMS), to produce SO4•−, which has strong oxidizing power. This study focused on determining the optimal preparation conditions, characterization of the catalyst, and investigating the effects of various inorganic anions on the degradation of Rhodamine B (RhB) in the Co/Fe-PMS system. The optimal catalyst preparation condition was found to be a 0.5 mol/L impregnation concentration, with the best ratio of Co(NO3)2 to FeSO4 solution being 7:3. The presence of Co and Fe in the catalyst was determined through FTIR and XRD analyses. The catalyst is a porous material with magnetic properties and is capable of degrading more than 95% of RhB within two minutes. It was found that H₂PO₄⁻, Cl⁻, and HCO₃⁻ had negative impacts on the degradation of RhB. Low concentrations of NO₃⁻ had a positive effect, whereas high concentrations of NO₃⁻ had a negative effect. This study presents a novel method for preparing highly efficient Fenton-like catalysts and offers an effective approach for sludge utilization.
